title: Instrumentation dry-run: latency ownership, provenance headers, and dependency matrix
body:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures the outcomes of a small instrumentation "dry run" we ran against the token-serving path to validate ownership boundaries for latency metrics, to prototype a minimal provenance header scheme, and to sketch the dependency matrix that will drive dashboard composition. The goal is a lightweight, reproducible pattern teams can adopt before a broader rollout.

High-level decisions (proposal):
- Ownership model: instrument at service boundary and at the RPC boundary inside the runtime (three layers: client SDK -> gateway/router -> model-exec). Each layer records its own success/failure and duration. The owning team is the component that will act on alerts for that metric.
- Latency semantics: use wall-clock durations and tag with "latency.stage" = {client, router, execution, kv-cache}. Derive downstream quantiles (p50/p90/p99) rolled up by tenant and model.
- Provenance headers: introduce X-RW-Provenance header containing a short base64 blob of key-values: {trace_id, route_id, model_variant, kv_warmth_flag}. Keep size <128 bytes; fallback to trace-level tags if header not present.
- Lightweight trace anchors: prefer 1-2 span annotations per request: "received", "queued", "exec.start", "exec.end", and emit a compact event for cache-hit/miss.

What we implemented for the dry run:
- Instrumented router service with duration timers at entry and after batching aggregation.
- Added X-RW-Provenance write path in SDK and tested propagation across gateway -> router -> execution stubs.
- Created a small consumer in observability infra that maps provenance header into trace tags and a minimal index in the metrics pipeline to allow querying by route_id and model_variant.

Observed behavior / learnings:
- Header propagation: header was consistently present in internal calls, but third-party integrations strip unknown headers; we need fallback via trace tags emitted at the gateway.
- Measurement skew: client-measured latency vs router-measured latency diverge for bursty requests when batching delays occur. Root cause is that clients see end-to-end TTFB while router reports pure server processing time. Need to explicitly document the semantics for each metric to avoid misattribution.
- KV cache tagging: identifying warm vs cold required a small boolean in provenance; instrumented the cache sidecar to emit cache_warmness_time and a hit/miss counter. Querying by kv_warmth_flag reduced investigation time substantially.

Metric definitions (candidate):
- rw.request.e2e.latency_ms: distinct semantics = client SDK measured start->first-token-received. Tags: tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, region. Owner: product-sdk team (alerts: p99 > 1.5s for 5m).
- rw.router.processing_ms: router entry->exit excluding queue wait (when queue is measured separately). Tags: same plus batch_size. Owner: routing team (alerts: p99 > 500ms sustained).
- rw.exec.compute_ms: execution span start->end (model-internal). Tags: model_variant, quantization_profile. Owner: serving-runtime team (alerts: p99 > model-specific SLO).
- rw.kv.hit_rate: ratio of hits to lookups by route_id/model_variant. Owner: serving-runtime (alerts: drop below threshold for tenant routes).
- rw.kv.warmth_time_ms: time between last successful prefetch and request; useful to compute cold tail.

Tracing anchors and sampling:
- Keep sampling adaptive: always sample 100% of traces that emit error or cache-miss events; sample ~0.5% of successful traces by default. For high-risk rollouts, flip to 10% sampling for affected route_id.
- Ensure span names are short and stable: use canonical names: "svc.gateway", "svc.router", "svc.exec.<model_shortname>". Avoid dynamic strings.

Dashboard sketch (minimal cells):
- Global: e2e p50/p90/p99 by tenant cohort (interactive filter for route_id and model_variant).
- Router panel: processing p99, batch_size distribution, queue depth heatmap.
- Exec panel: model compute p50/p90/p99, GPU utilization correlated with p99 spikes.
- KV panel: hit rate over time, cold-request time distribution, hit/miss drilldowns per route.
- Investigation quickcards: top traces for the last 30m with trace links, top routes by p99 regression, recent provenance header samples (decoded).

Ownership handoff checklist (what to do when flipping from dry-run to formal):
1) Documentation: commit canonical metric table to Confluence and reference metric contracts in README.
2) Alerts: owners identify alert thresholds and runbook links.
3) Instrumentation: standardize SDK helpers for provenance header creation/consumption.
4) Sampling: deploy adaptive sampler config and run for 2 weeks to capture baseline.
5) Dashboard: create template panels and store JSON in observability repo for reproducible deployment.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Size/encoding of provenance header: is base64 key-value the right long-term API? Alternative: compressed protobuf. Action: security review for header payload content and size (OBS-421).
- Client ownership: where should end-to-end e2e metric alerting live — SDK product team or owning product team?
- Billing/metrics cost: adding per-request tags increases cardinality. Need a signal-cost impact estimate (rough calc required).

Immediate next steps (2 week sprint):
- (Liam) Draft Confluence page with metric contract + examples (due 2025-11-25).
- (Marisol) Implement fallback trace-tag propagation for external clients (PR in obs repo).
- (Ethan) Prototype dashboard JSON and runbook stubs; wire alert rules to a test oncall rotation.
- (Aisha) Coordinate security review and sampling budget estimate.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a short-lived provenance token (signed) rather than raw header to avoid sensitive info leakage.
- Could leverage existing trace context baggage for light-weight model_variant propagation if header adoption is slow.
- For dashboards, provide a lightweight "investigate" mode that pre-filters traces with kv_miss=true to speed common ops flows.

Appendix: quick command snippets used during dry-run:
- curl -> gateway trace: curl -v -H 'X-RW-Provenance: eyJ0Ijoi...'
- kafka consumer proto -> mapping: scripts/decode_provenance.py (see PR link)

End of notes.
